GUI.note:
Assessment
33-year-old female (MRN SYN-6198936) referred for confirmation of suspected polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) in the setting of oligomenorrhea (cycles every 60-90 days since autumn 2023; previously regular 28-30 days in 06/2023), hirsutism (modified Ferriman-Gallwey score 12), inflammatory acne, and mildly elevated total testosterone (58 ng/dL; normal DHEA-S 262 ug/dL, prolactin 14 ng/mL, TSH 1.8 mIU/L).

1. Clinical Presentation & Differential Diagnosis:
Although oligomenorrhea and hyperandrogenism can be seen in PCOS, PCOS is a diagnosis of exclusion. This patient's presentation does NOT fit uncomplicated PCOS and instead strongly points to endogenous Cushing syndrome (hypercortisolism), which must be excluded first:
- Rapid central weight gain: +14 kg in 1 year (70 kg in 06/2023 to 84 kg in 05/2024), predominantly abdominal.
- New, severe hypertension: BP 156/98 mmHg despite amlodipine 5 mg daily (up from 118/74 mmHg in 06/2023).
